tool_input.command: wc -l game.html && node --check <(sed -n '/<script>/,/<\/script>/p' game.html | sed '1d;$d') 2>&1 | head -50

wc -l game.html
awk '/<script>/{flag=1;next}/<\/script>/{flag=0}flag' game.html > /tmp/game_script.js
wc -l /tmp/game_script.js
node --check /tmp/game_script.js && echo "SYNTAX_OK"

node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const html=fs.readFileSync('game.html','utf8'); const m=html.match(/<script>([\s\S]*)<\/script>/); if(!m){console.log('NO_SCRIPT_FOUND');process.exit(1);} new (require('vm').Script)(m[1]); console.log('SYNTAX_OK, length='+m[1].length);"
for t in h1 h2 h3 h4; do echo -n "$t: "; grep -o "<$t[ >]" game.html | wc -l; grep -o "</$t>" game.html | wc -l; done

claude.result:
**ASHFALL OUTPOST is complete** at `./game.html` (1643 lines, single self-contained file, no other files created).

All 13 systems are implemented: seeded-PRNG core loop, 8×8 procedural map with terrain-gated buildings and adjacency bonuses, multi-stage production chains (ore→metal, ash→soil→food) with storage caps and overflow logging, individual colonists with skill/fatigue/morale, food/water shortages with recoverable morale consequences, a 10-node research tree, 13 weighted events (5 with genuine multi-choice tradeoffs) with cooldowns, a caravan with stockpile- and drift-based pricing, scaling ashstorms with mitigation/repair, JSON save/load with validation (no browser storage), win/lose/scoring, a tabbed+tooltip+keyboard-driven UI, and a Dev panel with 29 test assertions and a deterministic 200-turn benchmark with state hashing.

One caveat worth flagging: this sandbox's permission mode blocks all inline code execution (`node -e`, `node --check`, `python -c`, even `awk`/`sed` with inline programs all required approval I couldn't grant), so I could not actually launch a browser or run the JS to confirm it executes cleanly. Instead I did a thorough static verification pass — read the entire file top to bottom, cross-checked every `getElementById` call against actual/dynamically-created IDs, and confirmed balanced braces/parens and every HTML tag pair (div/span/button/table/th/select/h1-h4, including the ones hidden inside JS-built template strings). That review turned up and fixed three real issues: a destroyed Habitat was still granting full population capacity (now gated on hp>0, matching how Windbreak already worked), a garbled leftover status-line string, and a missing "labor" cost on repairs (spec asked for parts *and* labor — added a fatigue cost to the colonist pulled onto the repair crew). I'd still recommend opening it in a browser and clicking **Dev → Run Tests** and **Run Benchmark** yourself as the real confirmation, since that's the one thing I couldn't do from here.
